cohort: The study included 50 pregnant women, divided into a group with obesity (n=25, BMI >=30 kg/m2) and a normal BMI group (n=25, BMI 18.5-24.99 kg/m2), matched by age, socioeconomic status, and systemic health.
finding: Pregnant women with obesity showed a higher prevalence of periodontitis and higher salivary levels of TNF-a and IL-1b, and their children had lower birth weights, more frequently classified as low (<2,500 g) or insufficient (2,500-2,999 g).
birth_weight: Birth weight was measured as an outcome, with significant findings for 'low' (<2,500 g) or 'insufficient' (2,500-2,999 g) weight.
